source_text: ista verba transferre, tamquam ipsos in se transfiguraverit Apostolus, qui contemnebant dona Christi, velut sibi non necessaria quod veniam daret ille peccatis, quae ipsi legis admonitione vitassent
pass_a_gloss: That words transferre, tamquam ipsos in himself transfiguraverit apostle, who contemnebant gifts of-Christ, as-if to-himself not necessaria that/which comes daret that sins, which themselves of-the-law admonitione vitassent.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Augustine reports that Julian refers these words to ‘the Jews’ pride,’ as though the apostle had represented in himself people who despised Christ’s gifts as unnecessary for them.
They despised those gifts because he offered forgiveness of sins that they themselves had avoided through the law’s admonition.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
